blocks.text: Leo had played the violin in the school orchestra for a year, yet few people noticed him. During breaks he would wander off alone, listening closely to the hall's empty corners. A month before the spring concert, the music teacher complained that the brass section always sounded muddy. The players practised harder, but nothing changed. Leo finally suggested a simple test: he moved the brass chairs two metres away from the back wall. Their sound immediately became clearer, because the wall had been bouncing it back too early. On concert night, the teacher asked Leo to explain the new seating to the audience. "Sometimes," she said, "the best listener in the room solves the problem."
1. Why did the brass section sound muddy?
A. The players did not practise enough.    B. The back wall reflected their sound too early.    C. Their instruments were old.    D. The hall was too small.
2. What can we infer about Leo?
A. He paid careful attention to how sound behaved.    B. He wanted to leave the orchestra.    C. He led the brass section.    D. He found practice boring.
3. What does the teacher mean by her last words?
A. Careful listening can lead to solutions.    B. Only teachers can solve problems.    C. Audiences should stay quiet.    D. Musicians must speak more often.
